title: A Firm No: What the 3I/ATLAS Radio Searches Could See (EA-3I-ATLAS-PUBLIC-01 v1.1)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A public account of what the published radio searches of the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS could see, and of what the public was told they saw. It reports three findings from a public-data investigation run 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-06: a Google AI Overview that presented Avi Loeb's July 2025 'most likely natural', held at Level 4 of his scale throughout, as a later concession; a sign discrepancy between the positive drift window the Allen Telescope Array search documents and the negative drift its own stated acceleration gives a tone on the object, with a public FAQ that dropped the search's frequency and drift scope; and thirteen weak comet-frame features in public Green Bank data, reproducible and fragile, below every published detection floor and unreplicated. It argues that the published searches were built to rule a signal out at the least cost without doing the work ruling out requires, and says what would settle each question and what would not. The working record, code and numbers are the companion notebook, #1742.
content_type: Essay; public account of an investigation (Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute)
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). The investigation it reports was run by Lee Sharks with two machine collaborators, Claude (Anthropic) and ChatGPT (OpenAI), on public data (the companion notebook, #1742, records who ran what). The essay was drafted by Claude in session on 2026-11-06 under Lee Sharks's direction and revised on reviews by DeepSeek and ChatGPT, each point checked against the record (#1742, §13). Its angle, its ruling on the Overview's account of Loeb, and the decision to deposit are Lee Sharks's; what the essay claims is his decision.
methodology: An essay on the record of the companion notebook (#1742): every number and quotation in it is taken from the notebook, its files or the saved sources, with the notebook's frozen plans, null families and caveats carried over.
falsification_conditions: A quoted passage not saying what the essay quotes; the ATA's executed filter shown to keep the negative drift class; the thirteen shown to arise from a processing step the record omits; any falsifier of the companion notebook (#1742) that touches a claim the essay makes.

wiki_article: A Firm No: What the 3I/ATLAS Radio Searches Could See (EA-3I-ATLAS-PUBLIC-01, version 1.1) is a public essay by Lee Sharks, deposited in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 6 November 2026 for the Transactions of the Semantic Economy Institute. It reports a public-data investigation of the radio searches for technosignatures from the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS, run from 2 to 6 November 2026 with two machine collaborators, Claude and ChatGPT, whose full record is the companion notebook What the Filters Kept (#1742) by Nobel Glas and Orin Trace. The essay makes three findings. A Google AI Overview presented Avi Loeb's July 2025 view that the object is most likely natural, held at Level 4 of his own scale throughout, as a later concession. The Allen Telescope Array search filtered its hits for positive drift, where the drift its own ephemeris gives a tone on the object is negative, and a public account turned the search's bounded null into a firm no for 1 to 9 GHz. And thirteen weak comet-frame features in public Green Bank data near 1667 MHz reproduce under an independent implementation, sit below every published detection floor, and remain unreplicated and unexplained. Its argument is that the published searches were built to rule a signal out at the least cost without doing the work that ruling out requires, and it states what would settle each question, among them the Green Bank antenna's pointing record for one scan. Version 1.1 (6 November 2026) makes factual repairs in place: MeerKAT's search is added as a fourth, the comet's hydroxyl line is described in absorption and emission as MeerKAT recorded it, and Loeb's April essay is said to give probabilities for four of the anomalies.
